headline: GOLD SLIDES to $4,082 — Morning Rebound Snuffed Out as Oil Near $112 Firms FOMC Rate-Hike Odds Into Oct 28 Decision
snippet: Gold spot reversed a morning rebound and slipped to $4,082 per ounce on October 22 — a one-week low — as Brent crude held near $112 per barrel and revived inflation expectations hardened October 28 FOMC rate-hike odds. Silver fell 3.48% to $55.84 in its deepest single-session decline in three weeks; the paired selloff in both precious metals on the same session as a broad risk-off move suggests pressure is macro-driven rather than technical, leaving the $4,000 floor as the key level into the Fed decision.

headline: ENDURANCE GOLD DRILLS 50m STEP-OUTS at Reliance BC — 5.89 g/t Au and 0.19% Antimony; PEA Work Underway in Bridge River Valley
snippet: Endurance Gold (TSXV: EDG) released six diamond drill holes at its Reliance Gold Project in British Columbia's Bridge River Valley, expanding the Imperial and Lower Imperial Zones with 50-metre step-outs and returning structures including 5.89 g/t gold and 0.19% antimony over 5.2 metres from hole R26-132. At current antimony prices the antimony contribution adds approximately 10 g/t AuEq upside to such intercepts; a Preliminary Economic Assessment is underway with these results expected to feed into the updated resource estimate and economic study.

headline: RALLY OVER: Mining Stocks Hit a Wall as Copper and Silver Plummet — Rare Triple-Metals Selloff Ahead of FOMC
snippet: A brief October rally in mining equities came to an abrupt halt on October 22 as copper, silver, and gold fell together in an unusual same-session multi-metal decline, with major producers and royalty companies selling off sharply as oil-driven inflation fears firmed rate-hike bets and compressed the outlook for metal prices. The simultaneous weakness across precious and base metals is rare and reflects broad macro risk repricing ahead of the October 28 FOMC decision rather than sector-specific news.

headline: CANADA GROWTH FUND BACKS EXIRO-ORION to Take Over Vale's THOMPSON NICKEL Complex — C$280M Commitment Secures Manitoba's Biggest Nickel Mines
snippet: Exiro Nickel, backed by Orion Resource Partners and the federal Canada Growth Fund, closed an acquisition of 81.1% of Vale Base Metals' Thompson Operations — including the T1, T3 and Pipe nickel mines and a concentrator in northern Manitoba — with a total capital commitment of up to C$280 million; Vale retains 18.9% and a multi-year nickel concentrate offtake. The Canada Growth Fund's participation marks one of the most significant government-backed critical minerals transactions of 2026 and signals Ottawa's intent to maintain domestic nickel capacity in a sector where China controls the downstream.

headline: FORTUNA HITS 350m at 0.96 g/t Au FROM SURFACE at Lindero Argentina — Deeper Pit Extension Targets Mine Life Beyond Current Reserve
snippet: Fortuna Mining (NYSE/TSX: FVI) intersected 350 metres grading 0.96 g/t gold from surface at its Lindero heap-leach gold mine in Salta Province, Argentina — a depth-extension result strong enough to target a deeper open pit beyond the current production plan. Lindero has historically been constrained by the known resource boundary; a wide intercept at grades above 0.90 g/t outside the existing pit design confirms the system remains open and could add meaningful mine life at a project already generating cash at current gold prices above $4,000.

headline: C$12.7 BILLION: TSX Exchanges Record Nearly 1,000 Financings in Q3 2026 — Capital Markets Open Despite Gold Equity Selldown
snippet: Canadian stock exchanges attracted 996 financings totalling C$12.7 billion and 50 new mining listings in Q3 2026, according to TMX Group data released October 22 — confirmation that junior mining capital markets remain open even as gold producer equities lag bullion by historically wide margins. For explorers seeking to finance drill campaigns in Q4, the data signals that project-quality capital is accessible, with gold and copper exploration driving the majority of new listings on the TSX Venture.

headline: KLONDIKE GOLD WRAPS 2026 YUKON DRILL CAMPAIGN — Year-End Resource Update Targeted; Montana Creek Gold Royalties Added
snippet: Klondike Gold Corp (TSXV: KG) completed its 2026 drill program at the Klondike District gold project in the Yukon and is advancing a mineral resource estimate update targeted for year-end, which is expected to feed into subsequent economic study work. The company also reported additional gold royalties at Montana Creek, adding passive income optionality to one of the largest contiguous land packages in the Klondike gold belt; drill results will be released following the standard review and interpretation process.

headline: CONTRARIAN COPPER: Trader Known for Massive Aluminum Bet Makes LARGE WAGER on Copper — Pushes Against LME Inventory Surge
snippet: A large commodity trader known for a high-profile aluminum position has made a significant wager on copper even as LME copper inventories climbed 8% in a single week and headline prices softened, according to Mining.com reporting. The bet echoes the geographic divergence between COMEX-concentrated exchange inventories — over 70% of global visible copper stocks sit in COMEX — and severe physical tightness in European and Asian markets; the trade appears to be a bet on regional supply constraint repricing rather than a view on global abundance.

headline: INTREPID METALS CONFIRMS GOLD at MATTIE Target, Advances CORRAL Copper — 1,725m Drilled in Arizona on Two-Commodity Program
snippet: Intrepid Metals Corp (TSXV: INTR) reported positive rock sampling results confirming the Mattie Gold Target within its Arizona land package, while four drill holes totalling 1,725 metres at the Holliday Zone at the Corral copper project have been completed and the rig has moved to the new Ringo Zone. The dual-front update on a gold and copper project in a proven Arizona mineral district illustrates the multi-commodity optionality being built at Corral, which sits in the same structural corridor as several historically productive copper mines.
